'''Fuku?ji Shrine''' (?????????) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Utano|Q65260610|qid=Q65260610}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Fuku?ji-ch?}}, {{ill|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Q580186|qid=Q580186}}, {{ill|Kyoto|Q34600|qid=Q34600}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}.

It enshrines {{ill|Empress Dowager Hanshi|Q11573356|qid=Q11573356|lt=Empress Hanshi}}, consort of {{ill|Emperor Kōkō|Q440518|qid=Q440518}} and mother of {{ill|Emperor Uda|Q349267|qid=Q349267}}. Since Emperor Uda founded {{ill|Ninna-ji|Q1202871|qid=Q1202871}}, this shrine is regarded as the temple's {{ill|Chinjugami|Q97479976|qid=Q97479976}}.

=== History ===
According to tradition, its predecessor was {{ill|Fukagawa Shrine|Q11560019|qid=Q11560019}}, whose name appears in the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}, but it burned in the {{ill|Ōnin War|Q385676|qid=Q385676}} (1468). Later, in Kan'ei 21 ({{ill|1644|Q6920|qid=Q6920}}), {{ill|Tokugawa Iemitsu|Q314481|qid=Q314481}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Imperial Prince Kakushin}} rebuilt the shrine buildings. Since Empress Hanshi's mausoleum was nearby, they enshrined the empress, and it became Fuku?ji Shrine.

The shrine name is also said to derive from the fact that Empress Hanshi bore many imperial princes and princesses<ref>Kyoto City Tourism and Culture Information System - Fuku?ji Shrine</ref>.

=== Precinct shrine ===
As a subordinate shrine, F?k?jin Shrine (Matsuo Daimy?jin), enshrining {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=F?k?jin}}, is said to have been established in the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} for safe transport. At that time, ice was customarily offered from {{ill|Ice house (building)|Q253893|qid=Q253893}} in {{ill|Rakuhoku|Q11555800|qid=Q11555800}} to the imperial court, and workers sometimes died during transport.

=== Cultural properties ===
=== Important Cultural Property ===
[[??:Fukuoji-jinja_20071107_001.jpg|thumb|Main hall (left rear)]]
[[????:?????-02.jpg|thumb|Worship hall]]
The Kan'ei revival shrine complex (two buildings and one torii) is designated a national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}. Designated June 2, 1973.
* Main hall ({{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|Q3193781|qid=Q3193781}}, copper roof). Attached: one munafuda, two stone lanterns.
* Worship hall ({{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}}, copper roof)
* Torii (stone, my?jin torii)

=== Festivals ===
* New Year's Day festival (January 1)
* Nanakusa-gayu (January 7)
* {{ill|Setsubun|Q746798|qid=Q746798}} festival (February 3)
* {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|Q11261910|qid=Q11261910|lt=summer purification}} (June 30)
* Autumn grand festival (around October 18)
* Ohitaki festival (November 18)
* {{ill|Ōharae-shiki|Q11261910|qid=Q11261910}} (December 31)

=== Access ===
* {{ill|Kyoto City Bus|Q4858667|qid=Q4858667}}: get off at "Fuku?ji" stop
* {{ill|Kitano Line|Q10883224|qid=Q10883224}}: about 3 minutes on foot from {{ill|Utano Station|Q11449247|qid=Q11449247}}
